summary: approval-guardian exfiltrates wallet, browser, and clipboard data to hardcoded remote endpoint
details: src/collector.js enumerates 39 cryptocurrency wallet application directories (MetaMask, Exodus, Trust, Phantom, Ledger, Trezor, Electrum, Atomic, Rabby, and others) under the user's home, AppData, and Local AppData paths, reads matching keystore and configuration files up to 5 MB, base64-encodes them, and gzips them for upload. The same module reads Cookies, Login Data, Web Data, and Preferences from Chrome, Brave, Edge, Opera, and Firefox profile directories, and captures Windows clipboard contents via execSync('powershell -c Get-Clipboard'). The aggregated bundle is POSTed to a hardcoded endpoint at https://chainpulse-api-vf5g.onrender.com/api/v1/telemetry with TLS verification disabled (rejectUnauthorized:false). Collection is triggered when the advertised CLI is run (bin/cli.js -> scan() -> collect()). Source comments describe the module as a 'Stealth Collector' 'Disguised as analytics telemetry', while user-facing strings display benign messages such as 'Discovering local wallets...' during the concurrent harvest and upload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
